issue_body:
# Site-wide LCP regression — performance scores below 85 on all pages

**Audited:** 2026-10-16T13:15:16.524Z
**Previous audit:** 2026-10-15T13:25:38.234Z

## What changed
| Page | Prev perf | Curr perf | Prev LCP | Curr LCP | Delta LCP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| / | 80 | 79 | 3902 ms | 4021 ms | +119 ms |
| /about | 89 | 82 | 3332 ms | 4165 ms | **+833 ms** ⚠️ |
| /projects | 88 | 82 | 3325 ms | 4140 ms | **+815 ms** ⚠️ |
| /projects/note-structurer | 80 | 70 | 4263 ms | 5856 ms | **+1593 ms** ⚠️ |
| /projects/screenshot-to-primevue | 76 | 69 | 4697 ms | 6338 ms | **+1641 ms** ⚠️ |

TBT has improved across the board (home: 268 ms → 173 ms; all others now ~61–73 ms), so the JS-blocking issue appears partially resolved. However, LCP has materially worsened on every page, suggesting an image delivery or server-response problem introduced since yesterday.

## Likely causes
- Hero or above-the-fold images not preloaded or served without priority hints
- A CDN/cache miss or origin slowdown affecting image delivery
- New or larger unoptimised images (WebP/AVIF not being served, missing `loading="eager"` + `fetchpriority="high"` on LCP element)
- A render-blocking resource delaying paint

## Suggested actions
1. Identify the LCP element on each page (likely a hero image or large background) and add `fetchpriority="high"` + `<link rel="preload">` in the `<head>`
2. Confirm images are being served as WebP/AVIF from the CDN and that cache headers are correct
3. Check server response times (TTFB) — an origin slowdown would explain the uniform LCP increase
4. Run a Lighthouse trace locally and inspect the LCP sub-part breakdown (TTFB, load delay, load time, render delay)

## Visuals
No visual breakage detected on any page (desktop or mobile) — this is a pure performance regression.
